title: Pixelasset marking (a region of the artwork, not a colour of it)
description: A marking is the one thing a coat palette cannot express: the same source colour becomes a white patch in one place and stays brown in another, decided by position. This file is a record and a tripwire, never an input — the override mask is recomputed from the pack at ingest, because a committed override map would be the third-party artwork in another encoding. The recorded hashes and counts are asserted by the tests, so swapping the pack fails by name.

derive_from.description: The shipped coat carrying the marking, as a key of the pack's `coats`.

against.description: The shipped coat it is diffed against, and the coat a marked rendered_coats entry must name in `from`. Must be the warm one: derived against black, the black body palette already contains the marking's greys, the ink/reshade classification collapses and reshade jumps from ~1% to ~30%.

sources.description: One entry per sheet family, keyed as the pack's `sources` are. Separate because the families are separate artwork with their own ink ladders.

reshade_pixels.description: Override pixels whose colour the base coat already has. Should be a low single-digit percentage of override_pixels; a large share means `against` names the wrong coat.

ink.description: The derived ink colours, lightest first. Recorded for review and drift detection, not read to build the mask.
